title: A session-time lore producer leaves cache generation directories without the owner write bit, so the owner cannot delete the checkout
description: FILED, NOT BUILT. Relayed by team-lead 2026-10-13; opum-doc ruled under DEC-183 (g) that this rides behind the v0.14.0 pair (constitution Article 3), so it is not in LCLI-714. FINDING: a session-time lore producer writes cache generation directories without the u+w bit inside whatever checkout a Claude session starts in, and the owner then cannot delete that checkout. MEASURED 2026-10-13 by opum-desktop in its DEC-183 reader worktree .claude/worktrees/review-36 (a relayed measurement, not re-resolved here): .lore/cache/graph/ladybug/1/generations/8ab4c4c5.../ has mode dr-xr-xr-x and holds projection.lbdb (r--r--r--) and index.json (r--------). It was created at 14:26 local by the reader session itself; nothing ran in the worktree before the spawn. git worktree remove then failed with Permission denied after partially deleting the tree; the same happened earlier with review-28 and review-31. opum-workflow 0.15.8 session-start.sh and session-end.sh do not invoke lore, so the opum-lore plugin session module (or a lore CLI call it makes) is the likely producer, UNVERIFIED. QUESTIONS THIS TASK ANSWERS: (1) which code path produces the generation directories at session time, and with what modes; (2) are the read-only bits deliberate (immutable generations)? PENDING DESIGN QUESTION, for opum-doc: do not pick a fix. Candidate (a): generations stay read-only and lore exposes a supported cleanup. Candidate (b): a reviewer session skips the cache. Related prior knowledge: ladybug directories are read-only in test fixtures and need chmod before rm (see the fixture scaffolding note).

acceptanceCriteria.text: The code path that creates a generation directory at session time is identified, with the modes it sets, and the finding is recorded on this task
The task records whether the read-only modes are deliberate, citing the code or ADR that says so
opum-doc's design ruling between the supported-cleanup arm and the reviewer-skips-cache arm is recorded before any code changes
Whichever arm is ruled, a checkout whose session created a generation can be removed by its owner with git worktree remove, shown by a reproduction before and after

implementationNotes: CARRY FROM LCLI-724 (closed duplicate at grooming 2026-11-18): two facts from that record that belong on this survivor. (1) When git worktree remove fails with Permission denied, git worktree list no longer shows the path, so the leftover reads as clutter rather than as the residue of a command that half-succeeded. (2) The DEC-158 ownership guard refuses a session any write inside a worktree path, so even a session that knows about the leftover cannot chmod or rm it by hand. Related, measured elsewhere: LCLI-740 delivered lore cache clear as the cleanup workaround for these generations (landed #666), but DEC-208 clause 5 holds it until the pair ships, and the pair has not shipped. This is a carry note, not activity (grooming ruling D2).
finalSummary: Closed as SUPERSEDED by LCLI-705 and LCLI-740 per DEC-281 (a1) / ODOC-608 (opum-doc, 2026-11-18T22:49:37Z), which reverses the earlier option C. Generation directories stay 0555 and the inspector's immutability check stays as written: C would have changed a deliberate integrity check, which was unknown when it was ruled. The incident's cause is already fixed: LCLI-705 gates the pane producer since 0.14.0, and the review-36 observation of 2026-10-13 predates the 0.14.0 bump of 2026-10-19, so it ran 0.13.x or older. The remaining case has a supported path, lore cache clear (LCLI-740), shipping in the next pair release; DEC-208's worktree hold lifts then. MEASUREMENTS taken here before the reversal: the publish path is src/core/ladybug-lifecycle.ts lines 330, 371 and 373, reached through reconcileLadybugProjection (line 174) from any retrieval command; modes are staging directory 0700, database 0444, generation directory 0555, control manifest index.json 0400; the read-only bits are deliberate because the inspector classifies a writable generation as corrupt (lines 813-828). A live specimen in opum-desktop worktree review-125-3ae5ee2, created 2026-10-21 by lore 0.14.1, showed exactly those modes, so the defect reproduced on 0.14.1, though the manifest records the CLI version and not the plugin version of that unit. CARRY FROM LCLI-724 (its duplicate): (1) when git worktree remove fails with Permission denied, git worktree list no longer shows the path, so the leftover reads as clutter rather than as the residue of a command that half-succeeded; (2) the DEC-158 ownership guard refuses a session any write inside a worktree path, so even a session that knows about the leftover cannot chmod or rm it by hand. REOPEN CONDITION, verbatim: a lore at 0.14.0 or later leaves generation directories in a worktree where no operator session ran lore. Nothing was built.
